papers.title: Proposal of a Machine Learning Predictive Maintenance Solution Architecture
papers.summary: This article proposes an architecture model for predictive maintenance in industrial units compliant with Industry 4.0 standards, utilizing machine learning to detect degradation and minimize downtime.

papers.title: Anomaly Detection in Sensor Data with Machine Learning: Predictive Maintenance for Industrial Systems
papers.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive review of machine learning-based anomaly detection for predictive maintenance, focusing on industrial sensor data challenges and algorithms.

papers.title: Optimizing Wind Turbine Reliability through a Machine Learning Predictive Maintenance Framework
papers.summary: This study introduces a machine learning pipeline using SCADA data and Genetic Algorithms to predict critical faults in wind turbines, achieving high predictive accuracy.

key_findings.claim: The proposed predictive maintenance solution architecture employs machine-learning algorithms to model equipment degradation, allowing for early failure detection and reduced downtime.
key_findings.evidence: To model the deterioration of the equipment, advanced data analysis techniques and machine learning were used, thus allowing for the early identification of imminent failures and reducing system downtime.

key_findings.claim: Machine learning techniques automate anomaly detection in sensor data streams to proactively identify deviations and prevent costly downtime.
key_findings.evidence: Machine learning techniques have emerged as powerful tools for automating anomaly detection in the vast streams of sensor data generated by industrial systems.

key_findings.claim: A machine learning-based predictive maintenance pipeline optimized with Genetic Algorithms achieved macro-averaged accuracy exceeding 97 percent for wind turbine fault prediction.
key_findings.evidence: Compared to a majority-class baseline, the optimized models achieved macro-averaged accuracy exceeding 97 percent and $\mathbf{F 1}$-scores ranging from $\mathbf{8 5 \%}$ to $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$ across the five fault types, demonstrating their capability to capture complex, nonlinear relationships inherent in SCADA data.

overall_summary: This research overview examines three recent papers published between 2024 and 2025 focusing on machine learning applications in predictive maintenance. The first paper proposes an industry-compliant solution architecture using machine learning to model equipment degradation. The second reviews machine learning-based anomaly detection techniques using industrial sensor data. The third paper introduces an optimized machine learning pipeline for wind turbine fault prediction using SCADA data.
